Assiduous

uh-SID-joo-us · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Assiduous is showing great care, effort, and persistence in doing something.

The assiduous violinist practiced the same eight measures for three hours until they were flawless.

Worked Example

The assiduous gardener checked every single plant for pests each morning before breakfast, without fail.

Assiduous emphasizes steady, careful, persistent effort over time -- not a single burst of hard work.

How Assiduous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

thorough

thorough: showing great attention to detail

painstaking

painstaking: taking great care and effort

Antonyms

negligent

negligent: failing to take proper care

careless

careless: not giving sufficient attention to avoiding harm or errors

How Strong Is It? — careful → thorough → assiduous

careful vs. assiduous

careful vs. assiduous: Careful is a general, everyday word for taking care; assiduous adds a sense of sustained, tireless persistence over time.

thorough vs. assiduous

thorough vs. assiduous: Being thorough goes further than assiduous in one sense, emphasizing complete attention to every detail of a task.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — as-

prefix — as-: toward (Latin (ad-))

root — sid

root — sid: to sit (Latin (sedere))

suffix — -uous

suffix — -uous: full of, characterized by (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: as- ('toward') + sid ('to sit') + -uous together suggest 'sitting closely by' a task -- the careful, persistent attention assiduous describes.

Use the root in a new word: sedentary

Use the root in a new word: sedentary: Sedentary shares the same Latin root sedere ('to sit'), taught earlier in Part 2 -- though sedentary describes physical inactivity, quite the opposite feel of assiduous's busy persistence.
